Bayesian inference of the magnetic component in the quark-gluon plasma
FIG. 1. Illustration of the dominant microscopic degrees of freedom in QCD matter at different temperatures. At low temperature (T < Tc), quarks and gluons are confined into a gas of mesons and baryons. At high temperature (T ≳2Tc), quarks and gluons are fully liberated and dominant, gradually approaching a weakly coupled quark-gluon plasma. An intermediate phase emerges in the 1 ∼2Tc region where the chromomagnetic monopoles are the dominant degrees of freedom and lead to properties of a strongly coupled fluid as observed in heavy ion collision experiments.

Introducing the concept of the Widom line in the QCD phase diagram

Large mass extrapolation of the lambda parameter from the decoupling strategy.In the decoupling approach the intrinsic scale of QCD is extracted after matching Nf = 3 QCD and the pure gauge theory using three degenerate heavy quarks of mass M. This plot shows that the approach to infinite mass (with corrections O(1/M2)) agrees with the expectations of an analysis based on effective field theory. The Born configuration of the gg initial state tends to emit valence quark jets at high energy, but it also emits more gluon jets compared to the case of the u¯u initial state since the color factor for g →gg is 9=4 times larger than q →qg. Consequently, initial-state radiation from gg reduce the quark jet fraction, and thus the improvement factors for u¯u are slightly better than those for gg.
